question: A 16-year-old woman consulted for primary amenorrhea. It presents a normal female development of secondary sexual characteristics. The levels of estradiol and testosterone are normal. In the gynecological examination, agenesis of the vagina is appreciated. Ultrasound is performed and there is absence of uterus. The ovaries are normal ultrasound. No left kidney is seen. The most likely diagnosis is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Absence of uterus + agenesis of the vagina -> Primary amenorrhea -> 90% CHAIN: Normal estradiol and testosterone levels + normal ovaries on ultrasound -> Exclusion of ovarian pathology -> 80% CHAIN: Absence of left kidney on ultrasound -> Suggestive of renal agenesis -> 70% CHAIN: Primary amenorrhea + agenesis of the vagina + absence of uterus -> Rokitansky syndrome -> 90%
analysis: The presentation of primary amenorrhea with normal levels of estradiol and testosterone, along with the absence of uterus and agenesis of the vagina, is characteristic of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome. The additional finding of absence of the left kidney is also commonly associated with MRKH syndrome.
